Let’s talk about something that’s absolutely vital when you’re working toward any big goal— persistence.
Chapter Six is all about The Power of Persistence: Navigating Setbacks and Staying the Course.
You know, once you’ve shifted your focus from perfection to progress, there’s another big step on the journey: learning how to keep going, even when things get tough. Because, let’s be honest, setbacks and disappointments? They’re just part of the deal—no matter what you’re chasing.
The real difference between people who succeed and those who give up isn’t some superhuman willpower. It’s persistence. That quiet determination to keep moving forward, even when you can’t see results right away—or when things just feel uncertain.
But here’s a secret: persistence isn’t about grand, dramatic gestures. It’s more like a habit you build over time—almost like training a muscle. Every time you push through a tough moment, you’re making that muscle a little bit stronger.
Think about it this way. Picture your journey as a winding path through a forest. Some days, the trail is clear and easy. Other days, you run into fallen branches, or the way forward is hidden by thick weeds. The trick? Don’t turn back at the first obstacle. Instead, maybe you climb over, go around, or just take a breather before moving on.
So how do you actually build up that persistence? Here are a few practical ideas you can start with:
First, break those big goals into smaller milestones. Every small win gives you a boost of motivation—and reminds you that you’re making progress, even if it’s step by step.
Second, track your progress in a way you can actually see. Maybe it’s a journal, a calendar, or a simple checklist. There’s something powerful about watching those steps add up, especially on days when you’re tempted to quit.
And here’s another tip: expect setbacks. Seriously, plan on them. If you know that obstacles are normal, you’re less likely to see them as a sign you should stop. Instead, you’ll just treat them as part of the journey.
Want some real-life proof that persistence pays off? Think about an artist who keeps getting rejected. They don’t pack up their paints—they keep creating and sharing their work. Sooner or later, the right audience finds them. Or a job seeker who goes through interview after interview without hearing back. It’s often the person who keeps showing up, who finally lands that perfect position.
But here’s something just as important—be kind to yourself during setbacks. Everyone makes mistakes or hits slow patches. Instead of beating yourself up, take a moment to recognize the effort you’re putting in and the lessons you’re learning along the way. That little bit of self-compassion? It makes bouncing back so much easier.
Remember, persistence doesn’t mean you never feel discouraged. It means you choose to keep going, even when your motivation dips. Over time, this steady commitment builds real resilience—and gets you closer to the goals that matter most.
